user.text:
Migrate this Next.js project from Pages Router to App Router. The project currently uses the pages directory structure with two pages (index and about). You need to:

1. Create the app directory with the proper App Router structure
2. Migrate the pages from pages/ to app/ (index → app/page.tsx, about → app/about/page.tsx)
3. Create a root layout file (app/layout.tsx) with proper HTML structure and shared metadata
4. Remove the pages directory and any pages-specific files
5. Update imports and routing patterns to use App Router conventions
6. Ensure the migrated app builds and runs correctly

Keep the same functionality and UI, but use App Router patterns and file structure.

history.assistant:
The project now uses the App Router. It builds, and both pages load correctly on a running server.

New files:
- app/layout.tsx: the root layout. It sets <html lang="en"> and <body>, which used to come from pages/_document.tsx. It also holds the shared title, description and favicon, plus the viewport setting that was on the home page.
- app/page.tsx: the home page, with the same content as before.
- app/about/page.tsx: the about page, with the same content as before.

Removed: the whole pages/ directory, including _app.tsx and _document.tsx.

What changed in the code:
- Each page now sets its title and description with the App Router's metadata export instead of next/head.
- The layout sets the viewport with a separate viewport export.
- The internal links now use next/link's <Link> instead of plain <a> tags, so moving between pages doesn't reload the whole page.

Checks:
- npm run build finished successfully and built /, /about and /_not-found as static pages.
- I started the server with next start and requested / and /about. Both returned 200 with the right <html lang="en">, title, description and heading. For /about that's "About Us" and "Learn more about us".

Two other changes to be aware of:
- During the build, Next.js added .next/dev/types//.ts to the include list in tsconfig.json.
- Both pages still link to /contact, which doesn't exist, just as before the migration.
